detaileddescription.para: On single-core targets, volatile access is sufficient because interrupts imply a full pipeline flush. This compiles to a plain store — zero overhead.
On single-core targets, volatile access is combined with a compiler barrier to prevent reads from being reordered before the index load.

briefdescription.para: Memory ordering primitives for cross-core and ISR safety.

detaileddescription.para: Provides acquire/release semantics for lock-free data structures that are shared between CPU cores (AMP multicore) or between ISR and main context.

Compile-time cost model
When SYN_USE_MULTICORE is off (the default), the acquire/release functions compile to plain volatile reads and writes — identical to what the code would do without barriers. Zero overhead.
When SYN_USE_MULTICORE is on, the functions insert hardware memory barriers (via syn_port_memory_barrier()) at the correct points to ensure cross-core visibility.

listitem.para: STORE_RELEASE: All prior writes are visible before this store. Use after writing data, before publishing the index.
LOAD_ACQUIRE: No subsequent reads can be reordered before this load. Use after reading an index, before accessing the data it guards.
